'''James E. Brau''' (born 1946) is an American [[physicist]] at the [[University of Oregon]] (UO) who has conducted research on [[elementary particle]]s and fields. He founded the Oregon experimental high energy physics group in 1988 and served as director of the UO Center for High Energy Physics from 1997 to 2016. In 2006 he was appointed the [[Philip H. Knight Chairs and Professorships|Philip H. Knight Professor of Natural Science]], an endowed professorship.

Prior to joining the Oregon faculty, he served in the [[United States Air Force|Air Force]] and held positions at the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] and the [[University of Tennessee]]. He is a fellow of both the [[American Physical Society]] and also the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. 

== Personal life and education ==
James Edward Brau, son of James Ernest Brau and Rose (née Nist) Brau, was born in 1946 in [[Tacoma, Washington]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=1969-05-26 |title=AF Academy to Graduate 3 from Area |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-tribune-af-academy-to-graduate/155430175/ |access-date=2026-06-09 |work=The News Tribune |pages=6}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Fulda Families - pafg1342 - Generated by Personal Ancestral File |url=https://fuldaohio.org/genealogy/pafg1342.htm |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=fuldaohio.org}}</ref> He married Mary Williams in 1969. They have two adult sons (Benjamin and Daniel) and four grandchildren (Alex, Judson, Sarah, and Beckett).<ref>{{Cite news |date=2011-03-10 |title=Rose M. Brau |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-tribune-rose-m-brau/160816811/ |access-date=2026-06-11 |work=The News Tribune |pages=4}}</ref> 

Following his junior year at [[Lincoln High School (Tacoma, Washington)|Lincoln High School]], Brau participated in 1964 [[National Science Foundation|NSF]]-sponsored summer program at the [[University of Puget Sound]], supervised by Prof. Z.F. Daneš, taking detailed gravitometer measurements of the [[Puget Sound]] area. He prepared a "Gravity map of Tacoma area, Washington (unpublished), University of Puget Sound, Tacoma, 1964", which contributed to his first scientific publication in 1965.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Daneš |first1=Z. F. |last2=Bonno |first2=M. M. |last3=Brau |first3=E. |last4=Gilham |first4=W. D. |last5=Hoffman |first5=T. F. |last6=Johansen |first6=D. |last7=Jones |first7=M. H. |last8=Malfait |first8=B. |last9=Masten |first9=J. |last10=Teague |first10=G. O. |date=1965 |title=Geophysical investigation of the southern Puget Sound area, Washington |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1029/JZ070i022p05573 |journal=Journal of Geophysical Research |language=en |volume=70 |issue=22 |pages=5573–5580 |doi=10.1029/JZ070i022p05573 |bibcode=1965JGR....70.5573D |issn=2156-2202|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Brau served as student body president at Lincoln High School in Tacoma,<ref>{{Cite news |date=1964-11-11 |title=Liberty Shrine Presented to Lincoln High |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-tribune-liberty-shrine-presente/155453173/ |access-date=2024-09-17 |work=The News Tribune |page=16}}</ref> where he graduated in 1965.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1965-06-15 |title='Frontiers' of Mind, Spirit and Heart Yet to Be Conquered, 1965 Lincoln Graduates Told |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-tribune-frontiers-of-mind-sp/155453084/ |access-date=2024-09-17 |work=The News Tribune |page=4}}</ref> He received an appointment from [[Thor C. Tollefson|Rep. Thor Tollefson]] to the [[United States Air Force Academy]] (USAFA),<ref>{{Cite news |date=1965-06-28 |title=8 Appointed to Academies |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-tribune-8-appointed-to-academie/86102208/ |access-date=2024-09-16 |work=The News Tribune |page=4}}</ref> where he double-majored in physics and mathematics, and was a member of [[Pi Mu Epsilon]] mathematics honorary fraternity.<ref>{{Cite journal |year=1968 |title=Initiates |url=https://www.pme-math.org/journal/issues/PMEJ.Vol.4.No.9.pdf |journal=Pi Mu Epsilon Journal |volume=4 |issue=9 |page=39}}</ref> 

On the USAFA Superintendent's List for academic and military excellence, Brau was also a member of Academy Student Section of [[American Institute of Physics]], a member of [[Pi Mu Epsilon]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=1969-07-13 |title=Dad reads Wedding Rites for Daughter |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-tribune-dad-reads-wedding-rites/113730146/ |access-date=2026-06-09 |work=The News Tribune |pages=79}}</ref> and he earned the [[George Owen Squier|Maj. Gen. George O. Squier]] Award as outstanding cadet in physics.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=2016 Fellows Summer Workshop |url=http://www.hertzfoundation.org/dx/newsevents/event.aspx?d=56 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170829123241/http://hertzfoundation.org/dx/newsevents/event.aspx?d=56 |archive-date=August 29, 2017 |access-date=May 7, 2016 |website=www.hertzfoundation.org}}</ref> Brau earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] in 1969 as a Distinguished Graduate of the U.S. Air Force Academy.<ref name=":3" />

Brau earned a ''[[Scientiæ Magister]]'' degree in physics in 1970 at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], working with advisor [[Irwin A.Pless|Irwin A. Pless]]. Brau's Master's thesis, ''Prism Plot: A New Analysis of Multibody Final States'' was published in 1971.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Brau |first1=J. E. |last2=Dao |first2=F. T. |last3=Hodous |first3=M. A. |date=1971-11-22 |title=Prism Plot: A New Analysis of Multibody Final States |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.27.1481 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=27 |issue=21 |pages=1481–1485 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.27.1481 |bibcode=1971PhRvL..27.1481B |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription }}</ref> While serving at Kirtland AFB, Brau took graduate classes at the [[University of New Mexico]] in 1972–1973.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2025 |title=Curriculum vitae, James E. Brau |url=http://pages.uoregon.edu/jimbrau/braucv.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251206230334/https://pages.uoregon.edu/jimbrau/braucv.pdf |archive-date=Dec 6, 2025 |access-date=June 9, 2026 |website=University of Oregon}}</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current citation is to curriculum vitae.|date=June 2026}}

Brau received [[Hertz Foundation|Fannie and John Hertz Foundation]] Fellowships (1969–1970 and 1974–77).<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=James Brau |url=http://hertzfoundation.org/fellows/fellow-profile/10317/James-Brau |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423235053/https://www.hertzfoundation.org/person/james-brau/April |archive-date=April 23, 2023 |access-date=2017-08-20 |website=hertzfoundation.org |language=en}}</ref> Based on data collected at the [[Fermilab|Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]] with research advisor [[Richard K. Yamamoto]], in January 1978 Brau earned a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in physics at MIT.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Brau |first1=James |title=Inclusive and Semi-Inclusive Charge Structure in Pion-Proton Multiparticle Production Reactions at 150 Gev/c |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252867372 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251207232855/https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252867372_Inclusive_and_Semi-Inclusive_Charge_Structure_in_Pion-Proton_Multiparticle_Production_Reactions_at_150_Gevc |archive-date=2025-12-07 |access-date=2026-06-09 |website=ResearchGate |date=January 1978 |language=en}}</ref>

== Career and research ==

=== U.S. Air Force (1970–1974) ===
Brau served in the Guidance Test Directorate at [[Holloman Air Force Base]] (1970–1971), and in the Theoretical Branch of the [[Air Force Research Laboratory|Air Force Weapons Laboratory]] at [[Kirtland Air Force Base]] (1971–1974), working with Gregory Canavan. At Kirtland Brau carried out theoretical studies of laser-target interactions, [[electromagnetic pulse]], and [[charged particle beam]]s. He served as chief of Kirtland's General Physics Group (1973–1974), and resigned his Air Force commission in 1974 as a captain.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Summer Workshop |url=https://www.hertzfoundation.org/event/2016-hertz-fellows-summer-workshop/ |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=Hertz Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Stanford University (1978–1982) ===
Brau was a research associate at the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] (SLAC) (1978–1982) in the hybrid [[bubble chamber]] experimental research group. There he was responsible for the hybrid bubble chamber facility's [[lead glass]] detector, in collaboration with colleagues from [[Duke University]], [[Florida State University]] and the University of Tennessee.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brau |first1=J.E. |last2=Butler |first2=J. |last3=Bugg |first3=W.M. |last4=Carroll |first4=J.T. |last5=Cautis |first5=C.V. |last6=Cohn |first6=H.O. |last7=Condo |first7=G. |last8=Dado |first8=S. |last9=Davenport |first9=F. |last10=Diamond |first10=R. |last11=Erickson |first11=R. |last12=Ferguson |first12=M. |last13=Field |first13=R.C. |last14=Fortney |first14=L.R. |last15=Franek |first15=B. |date=May 1982 |title=The lead glass columns: A large shower detector at the SLAC hybrid facility |url=https://inspirehep.net/files/af3f75a9c054c5c3bc2c97be70d6f635 |journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research |volume=196 |issue=2–3 |pages=403–413 |bibcode=1982NIMPR.196..403B |doi=10.1016/0029-554X(82)90105-7 |osti=1446127 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240917054734/https://inspirehep.net/files/af3f75a9c054c5c3bc2c97be70d6f635 |archive-date=September 17, 2024 |access-date=September 17, 2024 |last16=Gearhart |first16=R. |last17=Glanzman |first17=T. |last18=Goldberg |first18=J. |last19=Goshaw |first19=A.T. |last20=Hagopian |first20=V. |last21=Handler |first21=T. |last22=Hargis |first22=H.J. |last23=Hart |first23=E. |last24=Huang |first24=D.Q. |last25=Kelsey |first25=D.P. |last26=Lannutti |first26=J. |last27=Lucas |first27=P.W. |last28=Moffeit |first28=K.C. |last29=Maruyama |first29=T. |last30=Palounek |first30=A.P.T. |last31=Parker |first31=D.B. |last32=Rafatian |first32=A. |last33=Robertson |first33=W.J. |last34=Rogers |first34=A.H. |last35=Sugahara |first35=R. |last36=Takahashi |first36=K. |last37=Tether |first37=S. |last38=Walker |first38=W.D. |last39=Yamaguchi |first39=A. |last40=Yamamoto |first40=R.K.}}</ref>

=== University of Tennessee (1982–1988) ===
On the physics faculty at the University of Tennessee from 1982 to 1988, he continued investigations of photo-production of charmed particles and [[vector meson]]s at SLAC.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Abe |first1=K. |last2=Armenteros |first2=R. |last3=Bacon |first3=T. C. |last4=Ballam |first4=J. |last5=Bingham |first5=H. H. |last6=Brau |first6=J. E. |last7=Braune |first7=K. |last8=Brick |first8=D. |last9=Bugg |first9=W. M. |last10=Butler |first10=J. M. |last11=Cameron |first11=W. |last12=Cohn |first12=H. O. |last13=Colley |first13=D. C. |last14=Condo |first14=G. T. |last15=Dingus |first15=P. |date=1986-01-01 |title=Lifetimes, cross sections, and production mechanisms of charmed particles produced by 20-GeV photons |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.33.1 |journal=Physical Review D |language=en-US |volume=33 |issue=1 |pages=1–18 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.33.1 |pmid=9956437 |bibcode=1986PhRvD..33....1A |osti=1447743 |issn=0556-2821 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260311083521/https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.33.1 |archive-date=2026-03-11}}</ref> He joined the SLD Collaboration, beginning preparations for an experiment at the SLAC [[Linear particle accelerator|Linear Collider]]. He studied the design of a uranium calorimeter for SLD and in 1985 published an analysis in collaboration with Tony A. Gabriel — the first to show that despite earlier experimental work, compensation cannot be achieved with liquid [[argon]] readout. Using [[Monte Carlo method|Monte Carlo]] calculations, Brau and Gabriel showed the importance of low energy neutron interactions with the readout medium [[hydrogen]] to achieve compensation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Brau |first1=J. |last2=Hargis |first2=H. J. |last3=Gabriel |first3=T. A. |last4=Bishop |first4=B. L. |date=January 1, 1985 |title=Monte Carlo Studies of Uranium Calorimetry |url=http://inspirehep.net/record/213038 |url-status=live |journal=Nucl. Instrum. Methods A |volume=238 |issue=2–3 |pages=489–495 |bibcode=1985NIMPA.238..489B |doi=10.1016/0168-9002(85)90490-5 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240917054734/https://inspirehep.net/files/af3f75a9c054c5c3bc2c97be70d6f635 |archive-date=September 17, 2024}}</ref>

=== University of Oregon (1988 –present) ===
Brau joined the physics faculty at the University of Oregon in 1988, establishing the first Oregon experimental [[particle physics]] group to collaborate with Oregon's existing particle theory group.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://ria.uoregon.edu/2011/faculty-achievement/james-e-brau/|title=2011 Research Innovation Awards - Discovery and Connection|date=June 2011|website=University of Oregon|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130117022512/http://ria.uoregon.edu/2011/faculty-achievement/james-e-brau/|archive-date=January 17, 2013 |access-date=April 9, 2016}}</ref> During early years at Oregon, Brau's research continued to be based on the SLAC Linear Collider where he collaborated on the SLD experiment. He led the design, construction and operation of an innovative silicon-tungsten electromagnetic [[Calorimeter (particle physics)|calorimeter]] [[luminosity]] monitor.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Berridge |first1=S. C. |last2=Brau |first2=J. E. |last3=Bugg |first3=W. M. |last4=Frey |first4=R. |last5=Furuno |first5=K. |last6=Gioumousis |first6=A. |last7=Haller |first7=G. |last8=Huber |first8=Jennifer S. |last9=Hwang |first9=H. |date=January 1, 1992 |title=First results from the SLD silicon calorimeters |url=http://inspirehep.net/record/337695 |url-status=live |journal=IEEE Trans. Nucl. Sci. |volume=39 |issue=5 |pages=1242–1248 |bibcode=1992ITNS...39.1242B |doi=10.1109/23.173184 |osti=10178797 |s2cid=12582455 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170305002640/http://inspirehep.net/record/3376955 |archive-date=March 5, 2017}}</ref> 

During the active period of the [[Superconducting Super Collider|Superconducting Supercollider]] (SSC) Brau joined the GEM detector project. When the SSC was terminated in 1993, he was appointed project manager for the SLD vertex detector upgrade at SLAC, and led the project which produced a 307,000,000 pixel [[Charge-coupled device|CCD]] vertex detector for SLD.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Abe |first1=K. |last2=Arodzero |first2=A. |last3=Baltay |first3=C. |last4=Brau |first4=J. E. |last5=Breidenbach |first5=M. |author6-link=Philip N. Burrows |last6=Burrows |first6=P. N. |last7=Chou |first7=Aaron S. |last8=Crawford |first8=G. |last9=Damerell |first9=C. J. S. |date=January 1, 1997 |title=Design and performance of the SLD vertex detector, a 307 Mpixel tracking system |url=http://inspirehep.net/record/447469 |url-status=live |journal=Nucl. Instrum. Methods A |volume=400 |issue=2–3 |pages=287–343 |bibcode=1997NIMPA.400..287A |doi=10.1016/S0168-9002(97)01011-5 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170305002642/http://inspirehep.net/record/447469 |archive-date=March 5, 2017|doi-access=free }}</ref>

The University of Oregon established the Center for High Energy Physics in 1997, with Brau as founding director.<ref>{{Cite web |title=James Brau |url=https://www.hertzfoundation.org/people/james-brau/ |access-date=2026-06-14 |website=Hertz Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> Brau's research group participated in the NuTeV experiment at [[Fermilab]] and [[BaBar experiment|BaBar]] at [[PEP-II]] at SLAC before applying to join the [[ATLAS experiment]] at the [[Large Hadron Collider]] (LHC) in 2005. According to the University's ''Oregon News'', he headed "the large UO contingent of faculty, postdoctoral researchers and graduate students at the [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]]."<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |date=2015-04-14 |title=UO physicists to seek dark matter particles when collider resumes - Around the O |url=https://around.uoregon.edu/content/uo-physicists-seek-dark-matter-particles-when-collider-resumes |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240918225540/https://news.uoregon.edu/content/uo-physicists-seek-dark-matter-particles-when-collider-resumes |archive-date=September 18, 2024 |access-date=April 1, 2016 |website=around.uoregon.edu}}</ref> In 2012 he was a co-author of the 2012 ATLAS [[Higgs boson]] discovery paper.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Aad |first1=G. |display-authors=etal |date=21 December 2012 |title=A Particle Consistent with the Higgs Boson Observed with the ATLAS Detector at the Large Hadron Collider |url=https://www.science.org/doi/suppl/10.1126/science.1232005/suppl_file/ciocio-som.pdf |url-status=live |journal=Science |volume=338 |issue=6114 |pages=1576–1582 |bibcode=2012Sci...338.1576Q |doi=10.1126/science.1232005 |pmid=23258888 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240205232756/https://www.science.org/action/downloadSupplement?doi=10.1126%2Fscience.1232005&file=ciocio-som.pdf |archive-date=February 5, 2024 |access-date=February 5, 2024 |doi-access=free |hdl-access=free |hdl=11376/1489}}</ref>

Brau led the Oregon group into the [[LIGO|Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO)]] Scientific Collaboration in 1997. He was a co-author of the [[gravitational wave]] discovery paper in 2016.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=LIGO Scientific Collaboration and Virgo Collaboration |date=2016-02-11 |title=Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=116 |issue=6 |article-number=061102 |arxiv=1602.03837 |bibcode=2016PhRvL.116f1102A |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.061102 |pmid=26918975 |s2cid=119286014 }}</ref>

== Advisory panels, committees, and councils (1995–present) ==
Brau served on numerous advisory panels and review committees, such as the National Research Council Committee on Elementary Particle Physics, (1995–1998),<ref>{{Cite book |url= |title=Elementary-Particle Physics: Revealing the Secrets of Energy and Matter |publisher=National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine |year=1998 |language=en |doi=10.17226/6045 |isbn=978-0-309-06037-0 }}</ref> and as associate director for physics and detectors for the Linear Collider Collaboration.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-12-07 |title=Brau to help lead international effort on next-generation collider |url=https://news.uoregon.edu/content/brau-help-lead-international-effort-next-generation-collider |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=OregonNews |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.nationalacademies.org/read/6045/chapter/1 |title=Elementary-Particle Physics, Revealing the Secrets of Energy and Matter, National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine. |date=1998 |language=en |doi=10.17226/28839 }}</ref> 

Brau chaired the SLAC Scientific Policy Committee (2001–2004), and served on [[Fermilab]]'s Physics Advisory Committee (2002–2006). He also served on the [[DESY|Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron]] Physics Review Committee (2003–2007).<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2005 |title=PRC Members 2005 |url=https://www.desy.de/f/prc/Mitglieder_extern2005.pdf |access-date=Jun 13, 2026}}</ref>

Brau participated on the Department of Energy [[High Energy Physics Advisory Panel]] (HEPAP) (2005–2008,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Past HEPAP Membership |url=https://science.osti.gov/hep/hepap/Members |access-date=June 11, 2026 |website=U.S. Department of Energy {{!}} Office of Science |date=18 March 2025 }}</ref> on the National Research Council Board on Physics and Astronomy (2006–2009),<ref>{{Cite book |url=http://www.nap.edu/catalog/11960.html |title=Plasma Science - Advancing Knowledge in the National Interest |publisher=The National Academies Press |year=2007}}</ref> and on the HEPAP [[Particle Physics Project Prioritization Panel]] (2007–2011).<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 May 2008 |title=US Particle Physics: Scientific Opportunities - A Strategic Plan for the Next Ten Years - P5 Membefship |url=https://science.osti.gov/-/media/hep/pdf/files/pdfs/hepap_p5_report_jb.pdf |access-date=Jun 14, 2026 |website=science.osti.gov}}</ref>

Brau has served on the International Advisory Board, Physics at the [[TeraScale (microarchitecture)|Terascale]], Strategic Helmholtz Alliance, Germany, since 2007,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009 |title=Who's Who in the Helmholtz Alliance? International Advisory Board |url=https://www.terascale.de/sites/site_terascale/content/e7/e341/e343/infoboxContent547/whos_who-2009.pdf |access-date=June 14, 2026 |website=www.terascale.de}}</ref> and the International Advisory Committee, International Conference on [[Calorimetry]] in Particle Physics, since 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026 |title=International Advisory Committee |url=https://web.cvent.com/event/45985898-e3a4-451b-a9f4-cd103944fc32/websitePage:7517035d-b565-4ada-a94c-6dea7636ed23 |website=Calor 2026}}</ref> 

Brau co-chaired the organizing committee of the World-wide Study of the Physics and Detectors for Future Linear electron-positron Colliders (2002–2014).<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=International Organizing Committee |url=https://pages.uoregon.edu/jimbrau/LC/wwstudy/committee.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140527220416/https://pages.uoregon.edu/jimbrau/LC/wwstudy/committee.html |archive-date=May 27, 2014 |access-date=May 7, 2016 |website=uoregon.edu}}</ref> He has been a leader in the worldwide collaboration to design and build the [[International Linear Collider]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jim Brau - LC NewsLine |url=https://newsline.linearcollider.org/author/jim-brau/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908061852/https://newsline.linearcollider.org/author/jim-brau/ |archive-date=September 8, 2015 |access-date=May 7, 2016 |website=newsline.linearcollider.org}}</ref> In December 2016 Brau was named "Associate Director for Physics and Detectors" of the Linear Collider Collaboration, effective January 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2016 |title=Press statement LCWS2016, LC NewsLine |url=http://newsline.linearcollider.org/2016/12/08/press-statement-lcws2016/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191109060756/http://newsline.linearcollider.org/2016/12/08/press-statement-lcws2016/ |archive-date=November 9, 2019 |access-date=December 16, 2016 |website=Newsline, the Newsletter of the Linear Collider Community |publisher=Linear Collider Collaboration}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Upon graduation from USAFA, Brau was named the Outstanding Cadet in Physics of the Class of 1969.<ref>{{Cite news |title=The Falconews - Air Force Academy |url=https://www.coloradohistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=FNS19690604-01.2.6&e=-------en-20--1--img-txIN%7CtxCO%7CtxTA--------0------ |work=Colorado Historic Newspapers Collection |at=Number 31 |publication-date=June 4, 1969 |volume=11|quote=CIC Leon A. Wittwer and CIC James E. Brau are co-winners of the Maj. Gen. George O. Squier Award as outstanding cadets in physics.}}</ref> He was a [[Hertz Foundation]] Fellow for the duration of his graduate work at MIT.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Hertz Foundation Fellows|url=http://hertzfoundation.org/dx/fellows/fellow_profile.aspx?d=10317|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170305011703/http://hertzfoundation.org/dx/fellows/fellow_profile.aspx?d=10317|archive-date=March 5, 2017|access-date=May 5, 2016|website=hertzfoundation.org}}</ref>

In 2000, Brau was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], for "contributions to the development of particle detectors, particularly calorimeters and vertex detectors, and for studies of the properties of the Z boson with the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory#SLAC Large Detector|SLD]]".<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellows Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=James%20Edward%20Brau&af=true |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

Brau is a senior member of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]].<ref name=":0" />{{Better source needed|reason=The current citation is to curriculum vitae.|date=June 2026}}

At the University of Oregon in 2006, Brau was named [[Philip H. Knight Chairs and Professorships|Philip H. Knight Professor of Natural Science]], an endowed position funded by Oregon alumnus [[Philip H. Knight]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jim Brau, Department of Physics |url=https://news.uoregon.edu/expert/jim-brau-department-physics |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=OregonNews |language=en}}</ref>

In 2009 he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], for "distinguished contributions to the field of elementary particle physics, particularly for developing and applying new technologies to facilitate precision tests of the [[Standard Model]]".<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2009 |title=Brau, DeRose and Tyler elected AAAS fellows |url=https://uonews.uoregon.edu/archive/news-release/2009/12/brau-derose-and-tyler-elected-aaas-fellows |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100614175006/https://uonews.uoregon.edu/archive/news-release/2009/12/brau-derose-and-tyler-elected-aaas-fellows |archive-date=June 14, 2010 |access-date=May 6, 2016 |website=uonews.uoregon.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/elected-fellows|title=Elected Fellows - AAAS|year=2009|website=membercentral.aaas.org|publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science|access-date=May 7, 2016}}</ref>

In 2011, Brau received the University of Oregon Research Innovation Award.<ref name=":1" /> In 2012, he was chosen to deliver the Inaugural Presidential Research Lecture at the University of Oregon.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012 |title=Inaugural Presidential Research Lecture will explore the Higgs boson |url=https://uonews.uoregon.edu/archive/news-release/2012/10/inaugural-presidential-research-lecture-will-explore-higgs-boson |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230419060240/https://pages.uoregon.edu/digital/uonews-archive/archive/news-release/2012/10/inaugural-presidential-research-lecture-will-explore-higgs-boson.html |archive-date=April 19, 2023 |website=University of Oregon |publisher=}}</ref>

As a team member of the [[LIGO]] discovery team, Brau was a co-recipient of each of the following prizes: 2016 [[Gruber Prize in Cosmology|Gruber Cosmology Prize]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ligo Team Members {{!}} Gruber Foundation |url=https://gruber.yale.edu/ligo-team-members |access-date=2026-06-09 |website=gruber.yale.edu}}</ref>  2016 [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics|Special Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Special Breakthrough Prize In Fundamental Physics Awarded For Detection Of Gravitational Waves 100 Years After Albert Einstein Predicted Their Existence {{!}} Breakthrough Prize |url=https://breakthroughprize.org/News/32 |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=breakthroughprize.org |language=en}}</ref> 2017 [[Royal Astronomical Society]] Group Achievement Award,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gravitational Waves Researchers receive Royal Astronomical Society Award |url=https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/news/view/653009-gravitational-waves-researchers-receive-royal-astronomical-society-award |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=Cardiff University |language=en}}</ref> and the 2017 AAS [[Bruno Rossi Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=HEAD Rossi Prize Goes to Gabriela González & LIGO Team {{!}} American Astronomical Society |url=https://aas.org/posts/news/2017/01/head-rossi-prize-goes-gabriela-gonz%C3%A1lez-ligo-team |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=aas.org |language=en}}</ref>
